title: Code Migration Worksheet
description: Prepare your source code and a checklist for a manual language migration. The worksheet does not translate or execute code.
intro: The Code Migration Worksheet places a source snippet and the selected language pair beside a fixed migration checklist. It does not produce destination-language code. Use the text to plan a manual rewrite and record the checks that the eventual implementation must pass.
audience: Developers planning a manual rewrite and reviewers preparing a language migration
input: The existing source snippet, its current language, and the destination language you intend to implement yourself.
outcome: A plain text worksheet containing the supplied source and a generic checklist for types, library calls, error handling, and comparison tests.
review: The checklist is not tailored to the semantics of your snippet. Identify project-specific requirements and write the target implementation separately.
bestFor: Small migration planning notes, handoff documents, and keeping a source example alongside the tests a manual rewrite will need.
steps: Select the current source language and your intended destination language.
Paste a focused source snippet or load a supported text file into the editor.
Choose Create Worksheet to combine the source and a fixed migration checklist.
Save the worksheet, implement the translation yourself, and compare both programs with tests.
useCases: Preparing a review note before rewriting a JavaScript utility in Python.
Keeping an original function attached to a migration ticket.
Recording type, exception, and library questions before assigning implementation work.
Starting a checklist for comparison tests between an existing program and its manual replacement.
commonMistakes: Expecting the worksheet to contain translated code.
Assuming the generic checklist has analyzed the source semantics.
Treating a planning document as a tested destination implementation.
tips: Add any runtime-specific behavior the fixed checklist cannot infer.
Keep executable comparison tests next to the planned rewrite.
Check standard library differences against the actual destination runtime.
Use the preserved source as reference while implementing the target code manually.

faq.question: Does the worksheet convert programming languages?
faq.answer: No. It includes the input source and a fixed checklist. It does not generate a translated implementation.

faq.question: Why can I choose two languages?
faq.answer: The language names label the migration direction in the worksheet. Choosing a pair does not enable a compiler or translation service.

faq.question: Is the checklist specific to my function?
faq.answer: No. The same type, library, error-handling, and test checklist is used for each snippet. Add your own project-specific requirements.

faq.question: What file is downloaded?
faq.answer: Migration Worksheet saves migration-worksheet.txt, a text planning document that includes the source you supplied.

faq.question: Where is my migration input processed?
faq.answer: The worksheet is assembled in this browser. It is not sent to an AI model or remote execution service.

examples.title: JavaScript to Python planning note
examples.description: Source language: JavaScript. Planned target: Python. The output retains JavaScript and adds review steps; it does not contain a Python translation.
examples.output:
Migration worksheet: JavaScript to Python

A reliable automatic conversion is not available for this language pair. Use the source below as a migration worksheet and verify types, standard-library calls, error handling, and runtime behavior in Python.

Source
const count = 3;

Migration checklist
- Map data types and null behavior.
- Replace language-specific library calls.
- Recreate exception and asynchronous control flow.
- Add tests that compare both implementations.
